newsitem.title: USA: Pabst says to shut Milwaukee brewery, lay off 250.
newsitem.headline: Pabst says to shut Milwaukee brewery, lay off 250.

text.p: Pabst Brewing Co said it will close a plant in Milwaukee and lay off indefinitely most of the 250 people working there.
Brewing done at the plant will be transferred to Stroh Brewing Co of La Crosse, Wis., Pabst said.

The brewer said it told union officials of the shutdown on Thursday and said it will retain ownership of the plant "with the hope that we might, at some future date, be able to resume our 150-year brewing tradition here in Milwaukee."

The company said, "We regret this decision since it will result in the indefinite layoff of all bargaining unit employees and cessation of operations at the Milwaukee Division for an indeterminate period of time."
The brewer cited first-quarter results that showed the division lost more money than exepcted despite recent cost cuts.

The company said, "The losses at the Milwaukee Division have been mounting and the demand for our product has been diminishing at an alarming rate...We cannot continue to absorb these on-going losses."
Pabst said it already had shifted about two-thirds of its Milwaukee production to G. Heileman Brewing Co, as Stroh was formerly known, at the end of last year.
The shutdown will be carried out by the end of the year, the company said.
"Pabst products will continue to be brewed at company plants in Texas and Washington state, and through production contracts with other brewers," Pabst said.
